name: Prayer Window
summary: A prayer arch and a small sunrise. Familiar, quiet, and directly connected to prayer.
why: The broad arch suggests a place for prayer. A small sunrise anchors it to the rhythm of the day. Fewer, bolder shapes keep the idea readable when the icon gets small.
risk: The safest evolution, though the arch is a familiar symbol in this category.
source:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 108 108">
  <title>Prayer Window - Tunisian Prayer Times</title>
  <rect width="108" height="108" fill="#164E46"/>
  <path fill="#FFF8E9" d="M30 76V51C30 39 41 32 54 23C67 32 78 39 78 51V76H69V51C69 43 63 38 54 32C45 38 39 43 39 51V76Z"/>
  <path fill="#E8BC73" d="M44 62A10 10 0 0 1 64 62H44ZM44 66H64A3 3 0 0 1 64 72H44A3 3 0 0 1 44 66Z"/>
</svg>

name: Five Moments
summary: Five bold intervals around one day. One light segment marks a moment of attention.
why: Five broad arcs stand for the five daily prayers. Their circular rhythm gives the app an abstract identity, while one highlighted interval adds a sense of the present moment.
risk: The prayer meaning is learned; the ring can also suggest a timer.

name: Open Sky
summary: An open book becomes a pair of wings. A wider identity for prayer, Quran, and learning.
why: Two generous pages form a book and a pair of wings at once. The central fold keeps the reading connection clear, while the open silhouette feels light and expansive.
risk: It puts Quran and learning ahead of the prayer-time function.

</svg>

name: Courtyard
summary: A woven tile around a quiet center. Architectural character, without a building silhouette.
why: Four angular bands frame a central diamond, like a tile seen from above. The coral palette and crisp geometry make this the most graphic, pattern-led direction.
risk: It can read as a design or craft brand; prayer is carried by the app name.

name: Olive Shelter
summary: An asymmetric olive sprig with a warm seed. Soft, earthy, and deliberately unexpected.
why: Two strong leaves and a single olive create a living, asymmetric mark. The pale tile and olive ink offer a gentler identity with a Mediterranean association.
risk: It may suggest a wellness or gardening app before prayer.

name: Prayer Beads
summary: A bold loop of beads with a small tassel. A personal devotional object becomes the identity.
why: A few large beads, a visible cord, and a short tassel preserve the character of a tasbih at small sizes. Burgundy gives this direction a warm, distinctive presence.
risk: It emphasizes dhikr more than prayer schedules; the loop can resemble jewelry.

name: Qibla Fold
summary: A compass needle folded like paper. Precise, energetic, and strongly directional.
why: A tilted, folded needle expresses orientation and intention. Its sharp silhouette contrasts with the softer directions, and the two broad facets survive reduction.
risk: It may suggest a navigation app; this is a symbol study, not a new feature.

name: Tunis Taa
summary: A custom geometric ت, from تونس. A bold Arabic monogram with no pictorial religious symbol.
why: The letter ت begins تونس. A broad angular bowl and two square dots create a compact, local monogram that lets the Arabic language become the identity itself.
risk: It relies on Arabic recognition and the app name to communicate prayer.

name: Quiet Time
summary: A clock opens into a pause. A bright, modern identity for an app that protects prayer time.
why: The familiar clock carries the prayer schedule. Its open corner becomes a pause symbol, connecting timekeeping to the app's automatic silence during prayer. Acid yellow gives the mark a confident presence among conventional prayer icons.
risk: Without the app name, the mark could read as a focus timer. The silence feature is more prominent than Quran reading.
source:

name: Dayline
summary: Five appointments on one confident rising line. The next prayer comes forward in electric citron.
why: Five upright gates share a continuous timeline, turning the app's central job into one compact sign: keep the five daily prayers in view and make the next one clear. The diagonal gives a familiar schedule structure its own silhouette.
risk: The meaning depends on the five-prayer story; without the app name it can suggest a schedule or an equalizer.
source:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 108 108">

name: Reading Hour
summary: A folded bookmark with time at its heart. Quran reading and daily reminders share one compact symbol.
why: A solid bookmark makes the reading connection immediate. A clock is cut into its center, joining the Quran reader and saved reading position to the app's daily rhythm and reminders. Violet and fresh lime give the familiar page a contemporary character.
risk: Reading leads the identity; the mark may also suit an audiobook or reading-habit app.
source:

name: Dhikr Loop
summary: An open, asymmetric ribbon and a single counting marker. A bold identity for daily remembrance.
why: The continuous ribbon represents returning to remembrance. A single separate marker makes the act of counting visible without drawing a string of beads. Unequal curves and a cut shoulder create a sculptural mark that remains strong at launcher size.
risk: It gives dhikr priority over prayer times, and its abstract form needs the app name to establish context.
source:

name: Dawn Switch
summary: A wake switch becomes a rising sun, connecting automation to the start of the prayer day.
why: A short switch body meets a sun split by a clear horizon. The low, asymmetric silhouette links the app's wake alarms and automatic routines to dawn, without adding alarm-clock details.
risk: The sunrise can suggest weather; the switch shape needs the app context to convey waking.
source:

name: Verse Steps
summary: One continuous stepped ribbon and a next-passage marker turn Quran memorization into a compact modern identity.
why: A single connected ribbon climbs through three levels. Its next square stays slightly ahead, suggesting learning a passage, reviewing it, and moving on. The geometry is deliberately bold enough for a small app icon.
risk: It can read as progress or learning in general; Quran meaning comes from the app name.
source:

name: Sakina
summary: A dove settles into a broad protective wing. Soft blue and ivory turn the logo into a small moment of peace.
why: The bird is drawn in a resting curve, with one generous wing folding toward its body. It expresses the emotional promise of quiet prayer without a mute sign or a building. The cool wing and warm body remain one strong silhouette.
risk: A dove communicates peace more directly than Islam; it can also suggest a wellbeing or charitable organization.

name: Jannah Garden
summary: A flourishing canopy rises over a flowing spring. A garden-inspired identity for hope, renewal, and peaceful devotion.
why: Three broad leaves open above two flowing bands of water. The composition draws on the idea of a garden and a spring to suggest paradise and renewal, without claiming to depict it. Deep green, pale foliage, and warm water give the mark a calm, generous character.
risk: The leaf crown can resemble a lotus, and the garden metaphor can suggest wellness before a prayer app.

name: Sanctuary
summary: A warm prayer place held within two protective walls. An intimate space for stillness, drawn as a sculptural sign.
why: A folded wall frames an open interior, with a small warm plane at its heart. Seeing the prayer place from above makes this a symbol of entering a quiet space rather than another mosque silhouette. The open front keeps the gesture welcoming.
risk: The abstract room can suggest architecture or interiors; the app name establishes its connection to prayer.
source:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 108 108">
  <title>Sanctuary - Tunisian Prayer Times</title>
  <rect width="108" height="108" fill="#EEDDCB"/>
  <path fill="#593D56" d="M54 24L80 40V65L70 71V46L54 36L38 46V71L28 65V40Z"/>
  <path fill="#BD7650" d="M54 58L67 68L54 79L41 68Z"/>
</svg>

name: Dawn Thread
summary: A flowing folded stroke gives the prayer day a continuous, distinctive signature.
why: A single broad stroke rises, turns, and returns. Its movement evokes the cadence of Arabic calligraphy without spelling a letter, connecting prayer, reading, and remembrance through one daily rhythm. A mint fold marks the next turn.
risk: The devotional connection depends on the name; the fluid shape can also suggest music or movement.
source:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 108 108">
  <title>Dawn Thread - Tunisian Prayer Times</title>

</svg>

name: Blue Manuscript
summary: A golden manuscript medallion becomes a confident, compact identity for Quran and remembrance.
why: A broad eight-point medallion recalls ornamental verse markers and illuminated manuscript margins. Its open diamond and ivory center simplify that tradition into a bold mark, with deep blue and gold giving the app an unmistakable editorial character.
risk: It emphasizes Quran and devotional reading more than prayer schedules, and can also resemble a cultural institution's emblem.
source:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 108 108">

  <path fill="#EEF2DB" d="M54 46L62 54L54 62L46 54Z"/>
</svg>

name: Common Ground
summary: Two folded prayer rows and two points of light form a bold, welcoming geometric signature.
why: Broad aligned bands suggest prayer rows seen from above, linking individual routines to a shared daily rhythm. The two small diamonds balance the mark like the beginning and end of a day. Warm persimmon and dark violet make this direction unusually vivid.
risk: Its prayer association is abstract; the bands can also read as layers or a chevron emblem.
source:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 108 108">

name: Fivefold
summary: Five folded facets gather around a shared center. A compact geometric emblem for a day shaped by prayer.
why: Five distinct facets represent the five daily prayers. Their oblique edges create a folded, architectural rhythm, while the open center gives the mark room to breathe. One terracotta facet brings the next prayer into focus.
risk: The abstract geometry needs the app name to establish its prayer meaning, and can initially suggest a camera aperture.

name: Miim
summary: A custom geometric م, the first letter of مواقيت. Arabic identity becomes the entire symbol.
why: The compact head and descending stroke preserve the structure of an isolated Arabic miim. Broad geometry gives the letter a contemporary silhouette, while a gold face gives its head the feel of a folded plane. مواقيت connects the mark directly to prayer times.
risk: It relies on recognition of the Arabic letter and does not illustrate the app's functions by itself.
source:

name: Light Lens
summary: Two unequal fields of light, cut by a clear diagonal horizon. A striking identity for the changing prayer day.
why: An asymmetric lens separates into two luminous fields, reflecting the transition between daylight and night. The uninterrupted gap gives the small icon a strong silhouette, while the two colors suggest different moments within one day.
risk: Its link to prayer times is conceptual; without the app name it may suggest optics or an abstract planet.
sub1: Day and night in one rhythm
source:

name: Lantern Fold
summary: A lantern reduced to a folded jewel, with a small light held inside.
why: A faceted body and a floating cap turn the lantern into a compact emblem. The open center makes the light feel protected, suggesting guidance and moments of reading or prayer after dark.
risk: Lanterns may suggest Ramadan more strongly than year-round prayer; this is a cultural direction rather than a feature diagram.
source:

name: Sakina Hilal
summary: The Sakina dove rests within one generous crescent. The Islamic cue becomes the shelter itself.
why: A broad crescent wraps around the original dove without crowding its head or raised wing. The crescent and bird form one upward composition: a familiar Islamic association around a quiet, living center.
risk: The crescent can also suggest Ramadan or nighttime; the symbol does not communicate prayer scheduling on its own.

name: Sakina Mihrab
tag: Peace in a place of prayer
summary: The original dove inhabits a broad prayer niche. The architecture gives its calm a clear devotional setting.
why: A pointed mihrab surrounds the bird as a complete architectural frame. The open base and generous inner space keep it welcoming, while the recognizable Sakina silhouette remains the emotional center.
risk: The prayer niche makes the meaning clearer, but the smaller dove loses some detail at the tiniest launcher sizes.

name: Sakina Khatam
tag: A dove cut into Islamic geometry
summary: An eight-point geometric seal holds the Sakina dove in negative space. Its warm wing remains a separate accent.
why: The dove is carved out of the main geometric form, so the Islamic pattern and peaceful bird share a single silhouette. A larger bird fits within the solid seal, and the warm wing gives the cutout a quiet point of focus.
risk: An eight-point seal is shared across several artistic traditions; without the app name, the mark can also suggest a cultural or charitable organization.

name: Jannah Mihrab
summary: A living garden and spring sit within a pointed prayer niche, making the devotional connection immediate.
why: The original garden becomes a small sanctuary: two generous leaves grow inside a pointed mihrab, with a flowing spring across its threshold. The arch is part of the entire silhouette, while the retained forest, celadon, and gold preserve the garden's calm character.
risk: The prayer reference is clearer, but the arch brings the direction closer to familiar mosque-based app identities.

name: Jannah Courtyard
summary: An eight-point Islamic courtyard frame holds the original flourishing garden and its spring.
why: A broad geometric frame recalls Islamic tilework and the enclosed gardens of traditional courtyards. Three leaves and a short flowing spring remain the heart of the mark, giving the geometry a living center rather than making it a separate decoration.
risk: It can suggest an Islamic cultural or garden institution; the small foliage is less distinct than the outer frame at launcher size.

name: Jannah Hilal
summary: A generous crescent cradles a flourishing garden, with a spring flowing through its open side.
why: The crescent becomes the garden's protective outer form, rather than a small added badge. Three gold leaves open inside it and a flowing band of water crosses the lower opening, joining a familiar Islamic visual reference to the original hope-and-renewal idea.
risk: The crescent can emphasize Ramadan or the lunar calendar; its Islamic association is clearer than its prayer-time function.

name: Sakina Salah
summary: Sakina's dove carries prayer in its wing: a folded prayer rug becomes part of the bird itself.
why: The original dove keeps its gentle head and rounded body. Its raised wing becomes a folded prayer rug with a broad pointed niche cut through it. The prayer cue belongs to the silhouette, joining peace and salah in one emblem.
risk: The rug-wing is intentionally abstract. The niche is clearest at launcher size, while the small icon still reads first as a dove.
key2: A prayer rug as a wing

name: Sakina Quiet Joy
summary: A soft jade curve holds a warm golden circle in an open, gently uplifting composition.
why: The broad curve feels welcoming and settled. A small, off-center circle adds warmth and a touch of happiness. Rounded ends, gentle asymmetry, and generous space give the mark a calm, unhurried character.
risk: The abstract mark may also suggest wellbeing; the app name gives it a prayer context.

palette.name: QUIET JOY / IVORY + JADE + WARM GOLD

source:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 108 108">

  <rect width="108" height="108" fill="#F3ECDE"/>
  <path fill="#24594D" d="M28 52C38 60 49 63 60 60C68 58 75 54 80 49C82 47 84 48 83 51C79 68 68 78 53 78C39 78 28 68 25 56C24 53 26 50 28 52Z"/>
  <circle cx="62" cy="42" r="10" fill="#D9A55E"/>
</svg>

name: Quiet Joy Mihrab
summary: Quiet Joy's soft embrace rises into a generous prayer niche, holding the warm golden circle within an open, peaceful space.
why: The jade curve keeps its welcoming upward movement beneath a generous pointed mihrab. Two small openings separate the architecture from the soft embrace, keeping the interior light and spacious. The off-center gold circle preserves the original warmth and gentle happiness.
risk: The niche strengthens the prayer association, though the abstract interior can also suggest a sheltered person or a place of wellbeing.

palette.name: QUIET JOY MIHRAB / IVORY + JADE + WARM GOLD

name: Quiet Joy Dua
summary: Quiet Joy's welcoming curve becomes two gently cupped palms, holding an open space for dua and a touch of warmth.
why: Two broad jade palms preserve the original mark's soft, uplifting silhouette while making the prayer gesture visible. Simple inward thumb turns suggest hands raised in dua without detailed fingers. The warm, slightly offset circle adds hope and quiet happiness without depicting a person.
risk: It communicates supplication more clearly than scheduled salah. Cupped hands can also suggest care or generosity outside the app's context.

name: Quiet Joy Sajjada
summary: A softly curved prayer rug shelters a small warm light, carrying Quiet Joy into a place for salah.
why: Rounded corners and a short, gently splayed fringe give the rug a soft textile character. Inside, a warm light rests over the same welcoming curve that defines Quiet Joy. The pointed niche makes the place for salah clear.
risk: The compact rug may also read as a small protective emblem; the fringe and niche make the prayer connection clearer at launcher size.
